answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks using graph-based trust propagation. Bounded credit flows from verified seeds along interaction edges like a resilient vine, isolating an ocean of fabricated identities in low-trust graph partitions. An attacker must expend scarce relational capital to secure legitimate endorsements per node. Even at the zenith of adversary compute scale, synthetic clusters remain quarantined, though legitimate new agents face severe bootstrapping friction.
